'''Netia''' is a telecommunications company which owns the second-largest fixed-line cable television and broadband network in [[Poland]]. The company was founded in 1990 and the following year was awarded its first [[Concession (contract)|concession]] to provide local telecommunications services in the city of [[Piła]]. Three years later, the company built and opened its own first network in the city of [[Świdnik]]. The company reached 100,000 subscribers in 1998, acquired its current name in April 1999 and was listed on the [[Warsaw Stock Exchange]] in 2000. 

In the 2000s and early-2010s, Netia expanded through its numerous acquisitions of many regional cable television operators and telecommunications companies, such as the [[Local multipoint distribution service|LMDS]] operator {{ill|Pro Futuro|pl}} in 2006, [[Tele2]]'s Polish operations in 2008 and {{ill|Telefonia Dialog|pl}} in 2011.

In 2006, [[Novator Partners]], a private equity investment firm domiciled in the United Kingdom and owned by Icelandic entrepreneur [[Björgólfur Thor Björgólfsson]], acquired a large stake in Netia.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://investor.netia.pl/press,list,1429.html |title=Information on acquisition of Netia's shares |publisher=Investor.netia.pl |date= |accessdate=2012-02-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141222154607/http://investor.netia.pl/press,list,1429.html |archive-date=2014-12-22 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cityam.com/never-down-and-out-meet-rocky-business-world/|title=Never down and out: Thor Bjorgolfsson is the Rocky of the business world|date=2014-12-14|website=CityAM|language=en-GB|access-date=2019-12-09}}</ref> In 2007, Netia and Novator announced that they were going to build a 4th mobile network in Poland.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.abcmoney.co.uk/news/16200740896.htm |title=Iceland's Novator Telecom, Netia to launch 4th mobile telecoms network in Poland |publisher=Abcmoney.co.uk |date= |accessdate=2012-02-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120122175102/http://www.abcmoney.co.uk/news/16200740896.htm |archive-date=2012-01-22 |url-status=dead }}</ref> 

In 2009, Novator sold its 30.3% stake in the company to financial investors in 28 transactions amounting to 590 million zlotys ($164 million).<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://uk.reuters.com/article/netia-idUKLB84436620090311|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191209130231/https://uk.reuters.com/article/netia-idUKLB84436620090311|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 9, 2019|title=Netia confirms Novator sold entire 30-pct stake|date=2009-03-11|work=Reuters|access-date=2019-12-09|language=en}}</ref> In 2015, Polish billionaire {{ill|Zbigniew Jakubas|pl}} bought an additional 7.8 percent of the company from [[MCI Management SA|MCI Management]] for 158 million zlotys ($42 million), raising his stake to 33.7 percent and making him Netia's largest shareholder.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/poland-netia-mci-management-idUSL6N0WU05G20150328|title=Polish billionaire Jakubas buys 7.8 pct of Netia for $42 mln|date=2015-03-28|work=Reuters|access-date=2019-12-09|language=en}}</ref> In 2018, Jakubas sold his entire share to [[Polsat Box|Cyfrowy Polsat S.A]], which then went on to acquire all remaining shares in Netia in 2021.
